TeamPCP package wave stole credentials

Campaign: teampcp-2026
Date: 2026-03-21 to 2026-05-12 (52 days)
Actor: TeamPCP (group)
Impact: credential_theft, self_propagation

Synopsis

TeamPCP's 2026 package compromises formed a cross-ecosystem campaign against official open-source distribution paths, including PyPI, npm, Packagist, and CI/CD trusted publishing workflows.

Story

TeamPCP's 2026 activity is best modeled as a campaign family. The same actor label and recurring credential-theft patterns appear across PyPI packages, npm packages, Packagist packages, and CI/CD publishing paths.

The March attacks were surgical. LiteLLM, Telnyx, and xinference used import-time Python execution to steal credentials from developer and cloud environments. Telnyx hid its second stage in WAV files and used `tpcp.tar.gz` as an exfiltration marker.

The campaign then widened. Trivy showed repository and workflow compromise, while later npm waves used worm-like package rewriting, stolen npm tokens, and trusted-publishing abuse. By May, the same operating model reached TanStack, OpenSearch prereleases, Mistral packages, SAP CAP packages, and many smaller names.

Package records carry exact versions, hashes, and package-level exposure. This campaign record carries the actor-level continuity: credential theft first, package publishing second, and automation as the amplifier.
